Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication:  Knee pain.. 
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar and multisequence MRI of the right  knee without IV contrast.   

FINDINGS: 

JOINT EFFUSION:  Moderate knee joint effusion. Small popliteal cyst. 

ANTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT:  Intact. 

POSTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT:  Intact. 

MEDIAL MENISCUS: Intact. 

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:  Within normal limits. 

LATERAL MENISCUS:  Diminutive appearance of the posterior body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus suggestive of large radial tear in the absence of previous meniscectomy.

The meniscal body also demonstrates complex tearing involving the free edge and the undersurface.

Intrasubstance degeneration in the anterior horn. 

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:  High-grade and full-thickness cartilage loss involving the central to posterior aspects of the femoral condyle and tibial plateau, with mild subchondral edema. Small central and marginal osteophytes. 

MEDIAL COLLATERAL LIGAMENT:  Intact.

LATERAL COLLATERAL LIGAMENT COMPLEX:  Intact.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT: Diffuse mild thinning of the patellar cartilage. There is high-grade and full-thickness cartilage loss throughout the trochlea, maximal centrally and laterally, with multifocal subchondral bone marrow edema. 

EXTENSOR APPARATUS:  Quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. 

BONE MARROW:  No fracture. 
 
OTHER:  None. 


IMPRESSION:

1. Diminutive appearance of the posterior body and posterior horn of the lateral meniscus, suggestive of large radial tear in the absence of previous meniscectomy.

2. Moderate lateral and patellofemoral compartment osteoarthritis.

3. Moderate knee joint effusion and small popliteal cyst.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Medial knee pain. Positive medial meniscus testing. 
Comparison: [REDACTED]. 

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar and multisequence MRI of the right  knee without IV contrast.   

FINDINGS: 

JOINT EFFUSION:  Moderate knee joint effusion. No popliteal cyst. 

ANTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT:  Intact. 

POSTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT:  Intact. 

MEDIAL MENISCUS: High-grade radial tear at the posterior horn/root junction. Large degree of peripheral meniscal extrusion, with the meniscus projecting 5 mm beyond the tibial margin. There is also a horizontal tear of the meniscal body and oblique undersurface tear of the posterior horn. 

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:  There is full-thickness cartilage loss involving the weightbearing portions of the femoral condyle and tibial plateau, with mild to moderate subchondral bone marrow edema. 

LATERAL MENISCUS:  Intact.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:  Within normal limits. 

MEDIAL COLLATERAL LIGAMENT:  Bowing of the ligament secondary to meniscal extrusion. 

LATERAL COLLATERAL LIGAMENT COMPLEX:  Intact.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT: Diffuse thinning of the patellar cartilage, with high-grade and small full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial patellar facet. There is also multifocal cartilage fissuring of the lateral patellar facet. Partial-thickness cartilage loss is noted in the central and medial aspect of the trochlea. 

EXTENSOR APPARATUS:  Quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. 

BONE MARROW:  No fracture. 
 
OTHER:  None. 


IMPRESSION:

1. Complex tear of the medial meniscus, including radial tear at the posterior horn/root junction, with peripheral extrusion.

2. Moderate medial greater than patellofemoral compartment osteoarthritis.

3. Moderate knee joint effusion.

In the medial compartment, there is radial tear at the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. There is diffuse low grade and high grade chondrosis along weight-baring, non weight-baring medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau. There is no subchondral edema. Osteophytes 
 The lateral compartment, there is radial tear at the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. There is diffuse low grade chondrosis along weight-baring lateral femoral condyle. Focal high grade chondrosis with subchondral edema at lateral tibial plateau (about 1.8* 2 cm). Osteophytes are present.  
 The patellofemoral joint, there is diffuse low grade chondrosis (less than 50% thickness cartilage loss) along medial, lateral patellar facets, medial and lateral trochleas. There is no subchondral edema. Osteophytes are present. The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact.  
 There is chronic complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, at mid substance. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact. There is anterior tibial translation. 
 There is chronic partial tear of the posteromedial oblique ligament. Chronic partial tears of the medial and lateral collateral ligament complexes are suspected. The extensor mechanism is normal.  
 Large amount of effusion with synovitis is present in right knee including popliteus recess. There are multiple osteocartilaginous loose bodies (about 1-2.5 cm) in right knee including suprapatellar bursa and popliteal recess. The surrounding musculature is normal.   -- Moderate tri-compartmental osteoarthritis of the right knee by evidence of chondrosis, subchondral edema, cysts and osteophytes. 
 -- Radial tear at the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. 
 -- Radial tear at the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus.  
 -- Chronic complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, at mid substance.  
 -- Chronic partial tear of the posteromedial oblique ligament.  
 -- Chronic partial tears of the medial and lateral collateral ligament complexes. 
 -- Large amount of effusion with synovitis and multiple loose bodies (about 1-2.5 cm) in right knee including suprapatellar bursa and popliteal recess: probable for secondary synovial osteochondromatosis.

Findings: Mild - moderate knee effusion is noted. Normal medial and lateral menisci. No evidence of tears.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  Osteophyte formation is noted in all three compartments. Minimal fraying is seen in the medial and lateral compartment articular cartilage. No cartilage loss.  T T T G distance is widened and measures 18 mm. There is mild - moderate patellofemoral dysplasia. Lateralization of the patella is noted with resulting severe lateral patellofemoral degeneration and complete cartilage loss.  
Conclusion: Patellar maltracking with severe lateral patellofemoral degeneration.
